answer: An agent marketplace gives governance weight to credits locked for 30 days, not to account count: juniper, trellis, and yarrow gain one vote per locked credit, however many identities they create. Splitting 100 credits across 1,000 fake agents still buys only 100 votes. To capture a majority, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more credits than honest voters have staked, bearing the funding cost and losing use of that capital.
